sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “The Sound of Snow” and answer questions 11–14. Vocabulary notes follow the poem.

passage.title: The Sound of Snow
passage.credit: —Hayden Carruth · “The Sound of Snow” · from Collected Shorter Poems 1946–1991 (1992), Copper Canyon Press

lines.text: Snow falls in the dusk of Connecticut. The stranger
Looks up to the glutenous sky, and it is remembrance
That tickles the end of his nose like the fingertips
Of a child and remembrance that touches the end of his
Tongue with the antique purity and coolness of the snow,
As if this were almost the beginning, the first snowstorm
Fluttering between his house and the serious hemlocks.¹
And best of all is the sound of snow in the stillness,
A susurration,² the minute percussion of settling flakes;
And the stranger listens, intent to the whispering snow
In the fir boughs, earth’s most intimate confiding,
And he thinks that this is the time of sweet cognizance³
As it was once when the house, graying in old dusk,
Knew him and sang to him, before the house forgot.
In the last moments of day the earth and the sky
Close in the veils of snow that flutter around him,
Shutting him in the sphere of the storm, where he stands
In his elephantine galoshes,⁴ peering this way and that
At the trees in their aloofness and the nameless house
Vanishing into the dark; and he stamps his feet urgently,
Turning as if in anger away from an evil companion.
Yet when, like a warning just at the fall of darkness,
Yellow light cries from the window above in the house,
From the boy’s room, from the old sixteen-paned window,
The stranger remembers the boy who sits in the light
And turns the glass sphere, watching to see the snowstorm
Whirling inside. And the stranger shivers and listens
To the tranquil and lucid⁵ whispering of the snow.
¹ hemlocks — evergreen trees
² susurration — murmuring
³ cognizance — awareness
⁴ galoshes — rubber boots
⁵ lucid — clear

questions.prompt: In the first stanza, the stranger is vividly reminded of the

choices.text: power he felt during snowstorms in Connecticut
enjoyment he found playing in fresh snow as a child
relief he found in the winter snow in Connecticut
sensations he experienced during snowfall as a child

questions.explanation: The snow makes the stranger remember how it tickled his nose and touched his tongue, calling up the physical sensations of an earlier snowfall rather than an account of playing or finding relief.

questions.prompt: In the context of the poem, the personification in lines 13 and 14 serves to

choices.text: establish the stranger’s connection with the house
transform the stranger’s feelings about the house
illustrate the stranger’s dim memory of the house
reveal the stranger’s obscured view of the house

questions.explanation: The house is said to have known and sung to the stranger. Giving it these human actions emphasizes how close and familiar it once felt to him, even though that connection is now lost.

questions.prompt: The references to “the sphere of the storm” (line 17) and “the glass sphere” (line 26) create a link between the stranger’s
questions.explanation: In the present the stranger stands inside the sphere of a real storm. That image recalls the glass snow globe turned by the boy in the house, linking the current scene to a remembered moment from childhood.

choices.text: increasing confidence about finding his way
developing sense of control over the storm
growing disinterest in continuing his journey

questions.explanation: The snow had first invited pleasant remembrance, but now it closes around him, hides the house, and makes him stamp his feet and turn away as if angry. His response to the storm has changed.
